limitations: The remainder is an analyst allocation estimate for national household accounts, not observed median household cash left over, a complete minimum-needs budget or a saving rate.

Domestic category consumption includes nonresident purchases here and excludes residents’ purchases abroad. The central estimate assumes residents have the domestic category spending mix, applied to published resident household consumption.
Income and consumption use the household-only S14 sector. NPISH/S15 and combined-sector income are not substituted.
Gross disposable income is after direct taxes and transfers but before consumption of fixed capital; net income uses the source B6N series. Neither is the earlier equivalised median-income measure.
Food includes food and non-alcoholic goods; restaurant services are outside CP01. Home energy covers electricity, gas and other home fuels, not motor fuels.

Housing includes imputed owner-occupied rent and other housing services; dwelling purchases and mortgage principal are outside these consumption categories. Housing excluding energy is CP04 minus CP045, so home energy is counted once.
Household-consumption healthcare and separately sourced global out-of-pocket healthcare are different concepts. Global OOP values are not added to the CP06 component.
Only current-price inputs are added or subtracted. Chain-linked volume categories are not additive and remain outside the remainder calculation.
COICOP 2018 and COICOP 1999 are separate source classifications. Missing countries, years and components are not interpolated, carried forward or stitched across editions.

The allocation range is conditional on coherent published cross-border expenditure totals. It describes unknown category allocation of those flows, not a statistical confidence interval or all source uncertainty.
Published source accounts can have different revision vintages. Original flags and source-coherence differences remain visible; identities are never forced to balance.
Comparisons of remaining shares use the same definition and income basis. Original nominal monetary totals remain current million EUR; no household PPP or industry inflation factor is applied.
No industry demand scenario is automatically translated into household income, prices, welfare or a future budget.

methods.formula: Resident S14 consumption × selected domestic category expenditure / domestic total consumption; remainder = matched S14 disposable income minus this allocated amount.
methods.price_basis: current million EUR, same-country and source year
